**Area:** [App extensions & system integration](../COVERAGE.md#system) · **Apple:** [Intents](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/intents) · **Issues:** [`area:system`](https://github.com/kolabs-dev/isim/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Aarea%3Asystem)

## How isim implements it

- **Adapted:** isim's own Objective-C framework (`isim/frameworks/Intents`, `INSiriRunner.m`), with a Siri card.

## API

| API / feature | Status | iOS | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| SiriKit (Intents) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: the Intents framework (messages: `INSendMessageIntent`, `INSearchForMessagesIntent`; calls: `INStartCallIntent`; media: `INPlayMediaIntent`; lists and notes: `INAddTasksIntent`, `INCreateNoteIntent`) with their resolution results (success / needsValue / disambiguation / confirmationRequired / unsupported(forReason:) / notRequired), response codes and the handling protocols (completion and async forms). The simulated Siri understands fixed English phrasings and the structured `siri intent CLASS key=value` form (docs/SCRIPTING.md; no speech recognition) and runs the conversation in the app's Intents extension (`com.apple.intents-service`, `INExtension` `handler(for:)`, `IntentsSupported`) or in the app (`INIntentsSupported`, `application(_:handlerFor:)`; `.handleInApp` via `application(_:handle:completionHandler:)`): resolve, confirm (messages are read back), handle; `.continueInApp` / app-launch failures open the app with an `NSUserActivity` carrying its `INInteraction`. Intents UI extensions (`INUIHostedViewControlling`) draw Siri's card. `INPreferences.requestSiriAuthorization` (system alert, remembered; Settings > the app > Siri; the `com.apple.developer.siri` entitlement is required), `INInteraction.donate` / delete (Siri Suggestions in Shortcuts; Siri donates what it handled), `INVoiceShortcutCenter`, `INUIAddVoiceShortcutViewController` (phrase typed) / edit / `INUIAddVoiceShortcutButton`, voice shortcuts run by their phrase. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit, per iOS version). Payments, rides, workouts and photos: the rows below. Not in isim: other domains (car, restaurant, bills, ...), Contacts-based person resolution by Siri, `INInteraction.dateInterval` (no `NSDateInterval` in isim's Foundation) |
| Custom intents (`.intentdefinition`; `INObject`, `INEnumResolutionResult`, `INObjectResolutionResult`, `INIntegerResolutionResult`, `INDoubleResolutionResult`, `INURLResolutionResult`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: `isim build` generates Xcode's Swift classes from each `.intentdefinition` (enums as `@objc enum: Int` with their resolution results, custom types as `INObject` subclasses with theirs, per intent the `INIntent` subclass with `@NSManaged` parameters, its `…Handling` protocol with Xcode's selectors, the response code enum (custom codes from 100) and the `INIntentResponse` subclass with `code` and a factory per custom code) and copies the definition into the bundle; `INIntent`, `INIntentResponse` and `INObject` subclasses keep `@NSManaged` / `@dynamic` properties with their values (objects and scalars). Siri runs custom intents in the app or its Intents extension like the system ones: values from `siri intent CLASS key=value` converted to the parameters' types, missing values asked for with the definition's primary prompt, `resolve<Param>For<Intent>`, `confirm`, `handle`, and the response code's format string spoken with its parameters. `INTENTS_CODEGEN_LANGUAGE = None` turns generation off; Objective-C classes are not generated (the Swift classes are `@objc`). Tested (HelloCustomIntents: test_generated_intent_classes, test_custom_intent_in_app, test_custom_intent_with_siri) |
| Shared types: `INSpeakable`, `INObject` (`alternativeSpeakableMatches`, `subtitleString`, `displayImage`, the initializers), `INObjectCollection` / `INObjectSection` (dynamic options), `INCurrencyAmount` / `INCurrencyAmountResolutionResult` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: value classes with copying, equality, secure coding and isim's property-list form (amounts keep their decimal digits). Dynamic options: `isim build` generates `provide<Parameter>OptionsCollection(for:with:)` for parameters with `INIntentParameterSupportsDynamicEnumeration` (like Xcode); when the parameter needs a value Siri lists the collection's items as choices (section titles as subtitles), or takes a typed value that is not among them. A `CurrencyAmount` parameter is an `INCurrencyAmount`; Siri says it as "€9.00". Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_shared_types; HelloCustomIntents: test_generated_intent_classes, test_custom_intent_with_siri) |
| Vocabulary (`INVocabulary`, `INVocabularyStringType`) | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: kept per app in its container (Library/isim/Vocabulary.plist, per string type). isim's Siri has no speech recognition: before it sends an intent to the app it spells names (media and playlist names, people's display names, speakable strings) the app's way when they match a vocabulary string or one of a speakable's `alternativeSpeakableMatches`, ignoring case and diacritics ("cafe noir" → "Café Noir"). Pronunciation hints are kept, not used. Global vocabulary (`AppIntentVocabulary.plist`) is not read. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_shared_types) |
| Media: `INAddMediaIntent` (`INMediaDestination`: `.library`, `.playlist(_:)`; `INMediaDestinationReference`), `INSearchForMediaIntent`, their responses, resolution results and handling protocols | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: Siri runs them like the other domains: "add NAME to my PLAYLIST playlist" / "… to my library" ("this song": what's playing, `INMediaReference.currentlyPlaying`), "search for NAME"; resolve (media items, destination; `unsupported(forReason: .playlistNameNotFound)`), confirm, handle (`.handleInApp` runs `application(_:handle:)`; search results are listed on Siri's card). Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_shared_types) |
| Messages: `INEditMessageIntent`, `INUnsendMessagesIntent`, their responses, codes and handling protocols | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: "edit my last message to say TEXT", "unsend my last message" (or `siri intent EditMessage message=ID content=TEXT`): Siri names the last message it sent with the app (its `INSendMessageIntentResponse.sentMessage`); restricted while locked; `failureMessageNotFound` and the time-limit codes have their dialogs. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_shared_types) |
| Relevant shortcuts: `INRelevantShortcut`, `INRelevantShortcutStore`, `INRelevanceProvider` (`INDateRelevanceProvider`, `INLocationRelevanceProvider`, `INDailyRoutineRelevanceProvider`), `INDefaultCardTemplate` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: kept in the app's container (Library/isim/RelevantShortcuts.plist). isim has no Siri watch face or Smart Stack: the Shortcuts app lists the shortcuts relevant now first among the app's Siri Suggestions (a date provider's interval holds now; daily-routine and location providers count as relevant, as isim has no routine or region signals), titled by the card template; running one runs its intent or continues its user activity. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_shared_types) |
| Payments: `INSendPaymentIntent`, `INRequestPaymentIntent`, their responses, codes, payee / payer / amount resolution results (`unsupported(forReason:)`), handling protocols and `INPaymentsDomainHandling`; `INPaymentRecord`, `INPaymentMethod` (`applePay()`), `INPaymentStatus`, `INPaymentAccount`, `INPaymentAmount`, `INBalanceAmount`, `INAccountType`, `INAmountType`, `INBalanceType` and their resolution results | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: "send / pay NAME $20 [for NOTE]", "send $20 to NAME", "request $15 from NAME", "ask NAME for $15" (or `siri intent SendPayment payee=NAME amount=20 note=TEXT`); Siri reads the payment back with the confirm response's fee before sending it, as iOS does, and refuses an amount the app's resolve marks unsupported ("can’t do that with “$600.00”"); the failure codes have Siri's sentences. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_payments; HelloServicesObjC) |
| Ride booking: `INListRideOptionsIntent`, `INRequestRideIntent`, `INGetRideStatusIntent` (`startSendingUpdates(for:to:)`, `INGetRideStatusIntentResponseObserver`), `INCancelRideIntent`, `INSendRideFeedbackIntent`, their responses, codes, handling protocols and `INRidesharingDomainHandling`; `INRideOption`, `INRideStatus`, `INRidePhase`, `INRideDriver`, `INRideVehicle`, `INRideCompletionStatus`, `INRideFareLineItem`, `INRidePartySizeOption`, `INPriceRange`, `INPlacemarkResolutionResult`, `INDateComponentsRangeResolutionResult`; `CLPlacemark(location:name:postalAddress:)` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: "get / book me a [OPTION] ride [from PLACE] to PLACE [for N people]", "where’s my ride", "rate my ride N stars", "tip my driver $5", "cancel my ride" (or `siri intent RequestRide dropOff=PLACE pickup=PLACE option=NAME party=N`). Places are CLPlacemarks: Siri looks a name up in CoreLocation’s offline gazetteer (an unknown place has only its name), and the pickup is the device’s simulated location. As on iOS, Siri first lists the app’s ride options (INListRideOptionsIntent) as a choice, then confirms the ride (the confirm response’s option and price), then books it; the ride’s status card shows the app’s updates for 8 seconds; cancel and feedback use the ride Siri booked last. In Swift the CLPlacemark / CLLocation members and `partySize: Int?`, `usesMeteredFare: Bool?` are the Intents overlay’s (CLPlacemark is the CoreLocation overlay’s class). Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_rides; HelloServicesObjC) |
| Workouts: `INStartWorkoutIntent`, `INPauseWorkoutIntent`, `INResumeWorkoutIntent`, `INEndWorkoutIntent`, `INCancelWorkoutIntent`, their responses, codes, handling protocols and `INWorkoutsDomainHandling`; `INWorkoutNameIdentifier`, `INWorkoutGoalUnitType`, `INWorkoutLocationType` and their resolution results | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: "start a [5 mile] [indoor / outdoor] run / walk / cycle / swim / …", "pause / resume / end / cancel my workout" (or `siri intent StartWorkout name=run goal=5 unit=mile location=outdoor`; kilometers become meters). `.handleInApp` runs the intent in the app’s `application(_:handle:completionHandler:)` in the background; `.continueInApp` opens the app. The response codes’ raw values follow the order of Apple’s headers. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_workouts; HelloServicesObjC) |
| Photos: `INSearchForPhotosIntent`, `INStartPhotoPlaybackIntent`, their responses (`searchResultsCount`), codes, handling protocols and `INPhotosDomainHandling`; `INPhotoAttributeOptions`, `INConditionalOperator` | ✅ | ≤17 | adapted: "show / find photos [of PEOPLE or THINGS] [from PLACE or YEAR]", "show my NAME album", "play a slideshow [of my NAME album]" (or `siri intent SearchForPhotos album=NAME location=PLACE people=NAME terms=WORD year=2023`): a capitalized name is a person (resolved by the app, with disambiguation), other words are search terms. The app’s `.continueInApp` opens it with an `NSUserActivity` whose `interaction` carries the intent and response, as on iOS. Tested (HelloSiri: test_sirikit_photos; HelloServicesObjC) |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 17 and earlier) | ❌ | ≤17 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `INAccountTypeResolutionResult`, `INActivateCarSignalIntent`, `INActivateCarSignalIntentHandling`, `INActivateCarSignalIntentResponse`, `INAddTasksTemporalEventTriggerResolutionResult`, `INAnswerCallIntent`, `INAnswerCallIntentHandling`, `INAnswerCallIntentResponse`, `INAnswerCallIntentResponseCode`, `INBalanceTypeResolutionResult`, `INBoatReservation`, `INBookRestaurantReservationIntent`, `INBookRestaurantReservationIntentHandling`, `INBookRestaurantReservationIntentResponse`, `INBusReservation`, `INCallCapabilityOptions`, `INCallCapabilityResolutionResult`, `INCallDestinationTypeResolutionResult`, `INCallGroup`, `INCallRecord`, `INCallRecordFilter`, `INCallRecordResolutionResult`, `INCallRecordTypeOptions`, `INCallRecordTypeOptionsResolutionResult`, `INCallRecordTypeResolutionResult`, `INCarSignalOptions`, `INCarSignalOptionsResolutionResult`, `INDateSearchTypeResolutionResult`, `INDayOfWeekOptions`, `INEnergyResolutionResult`, `INFile`, `INFileResolutionResult`, `INFlightReservation`, `INGetAvailableRestaurantReservationBookingDefaultsIntent`, `INGetAvailableRestaurantReservationBookingDefaultsIntentHandling` and more (204 types, less those issue #411 added; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
| Types not yet in isim (iOS 18) | ❌ | 18.0 | not implemented, found by the 2026-10 sweep: `INMessageReaction`, `INMessageReactionType`, `INSticker` (3 types; with their members under "Not yet in isim") |
